question_text:
Using monochromatic radiation of wavelength λ = 0.1937 nm and given that FCC Ni has a lattice parameter a = 0.3524 nm, determine the first‐order diffraction angle (2θ) for the (111) planes.

"Table 3.1
Atomic Radii and Crystal Structures for 16 Metals
\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|l|l|l|}
\hline Metal & Crystal Structure ${ }^a$ & Atomic Radius ${ }^{\text {b }}$ (nm) & Metal & Crystal Structure & Atomic Radius (nm) \\
\hline Aluminum & FCC & 0.1431 & Molybdenum & BCC & 0.1363 \\
\hline Cadmium & HCP & 0.1490 & Nickel & FCC & 0.1246 \\
\hline Chromium & BCC & 0.1249 & Platinum & FCC & 0.1387 \\
\hline Cobalt & HCP & 0.1253 & Silver & FCC & 0.1445 \\
\hline Copper & FCC & 0.1278 & Tantalum & BCC & 0.1430 \\
\hline Gold & FCC & 0.1442 & Titanium ( $\alpha$ ) & HCP & 0.1445 \\
\hline Iron ( $\alpha$ ) & BCC & 0.1241 & Tungsten & BCC & 0.1371 \\
\hline Lead & FCC & 0.1750 & Zinc & HCP & 0.1332 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
${ }^a$ FCC $=$ face-centered cubic; HCP $=$ hexagonal close-packed; $\mathrm{BCC}=$ body-centered cubic. ${ }^b \mathrm{~A}$ nanometer (nm) equals $10^{-9} \mathrm{~m}$; to convert from nanometers to angstrom units ( $\AA$ ), multiply the nanometer value by 10 ."The unit of the answer is ${\circ}$.
response:
Using Bragg's law for first-order diffraction (n = 1):

$$n\lambda = 2d_{hkl}\sin\theta$$

For a cubic crystal, the interplanar spacing is:

$$d_{hkl} = \frac{a}{\sqrt{h^2+k^2+l^2}} = \frac{0.3524}{\sqrt{3}} = 0.20346\text{ nm}$$

Then:

$$\sin\theta = \frac{\lambda}{2d} = \frac{0.1937}{2(0.20346)} = 0.4760$$

$$\theta = \arcsin(0.4760) = 28.43°$$

$$2\theta = 56.85°$$

$$\boxed{56.85}$$
